subject: music-technology
intro: Music technology leads into the studios, stages and broadcast chains where sound is captured, shaped and delivered — the engineers and technicians behind records, live shows, media scores and transmissions.

roles.title: Sound Engineering Technicians
roles.entry: Postsecondary nondegree award or associate's degree
roles.what: Assemble and operate equipment to record, synchronise, mix, edit or reproduce sound — music, voices and sound effects — for records, theatre, video, film, television and podcasts.
roles.where: Units 1 and 2 are the core craft: microphones and placement, signal flow and gain staging, then EQ, compression, balance, panning and depth in the mix, finished by unit 6's mastering chain.

roles.title: Audio and Video Technicians
roles.what: Set up, maintain and dismantle audio and video equipment — microphones, speakers, cables, mixing boards, cameras and monitors — for concerts, conventions, presentations and other live or recorded events.
roles.where: Unit 1's microphones, signal flow and capturing a performance map straight onto live event work, with unit 2's critical listening habits and unit 4's DAW editing for recorded deliverables.

roles.title: Broadcast Technicians
roles.what: Set up, operate and maintain the electronic equipment that acquires, edits and transmits audio and video for radio and television, regulating signal strength, clarity and volume on air.
roles.where: Unit 4's DAW architecture and automation and unit 6's loudness, streaming standards and delivery formats are the technical discipline broadcast chains run on every day.

roles.title: Music Directors and Composers
roles.what: Conduct, direct, plan and lead performances by musical groups, or create original works of music for ensembles, productions and media projects.
roles.where: Unit 3's synthesis, sampling and MIDI sequencing is the modern composer's instrument set, and unit 5's genre production signatures teaches the stylistic vocabulary this work trades in.
